Our stories have been told through music and movies, and the practitioners have transcended from fathers and mothers to children. In this piece, SAMUEL ABULUDE writes on how some entertainers have entrenched their legacy beyond themselves.
The Nigerian entertainment landscape has a rich history of dynastic success, where creative genius, performance art, and entrepreneurial grit have been successfully passed down from legendary icons to their children.
Several prominent Nigerian families have built true entertainment empires across music, film, and television, with the next generation stepping up to carry the torch.
Adeyemi Afolayan known as Ade Love was a titan of early Nigerian cinema, renowned for his stage and screen contributions in the golden age of traveling theatre and celluloid films such as Iyani Wura and Taxi Driver. Ade Love died in 1996, and the legacy was passed down to the children who have formed one of Africa’s most formidable filmmaking dynasties. Kunle Afolayan is an award-winning filmmaker, director, and producer of October 1, The Figurine and Aníkúlápó. Gabriel, Aremu, and Moji Afolayan are all established actors and filmmakers who have consistently graced the screen in both Yoruba- and English-language Nollywood.
The late Fela Anikulapo Kuti was a voice and a great pioneer of Afrobeat, which has inspired many beyond the African continent. Fela died in August 1997. His music legacy has been sustained globally by his sons.
Femi Kuti is a four-time Grammy-nominated saxophonist who leads The Positive Force band. Seun Kuti leads his late father’s legendary Egypt 80 band, touring the globe and carrying on both the political consciousness and sonic power of Afrobeat. Already, the Kuti family has spanned three generations of musicians, as Femi’s son, Made Kuti, has taken the cue and is propagating his own brand of Afrobeat.
Pete Edochie is a celebrated veteran actor known for his powerful interpretations of traditional royalty and deep wisdom on screen, which has inspired his sons, Yul and Linc, to take after him. He is 79 years old and still in the profession. Yul Edochie is a popular Nollywood actor and producer who has carved out a niche for himself as an accomplished actor. Linc Edochie is an actor and filmmaker who has also contributed significantly to the family’s acting footprint.
Adebayo Salami popularly known as Oga Bello is a foundational icon of the dramatic Yoruba film industry with decades of stage and screen history. At 74, the actor and producer is still active in the industry, having inspired many, including his sons Femi, Tope and Sodiq Adebayo, who are in the movie sector. Femi Adebayo is a lawyer-turned-actor, producer, and box-office force (King of Thieves, Jagun Jagun) who have made a mark in contemporary Nollywood. Tope Adebayo and Sodiq Adebayo are accomplished directors, actors, and producers known in the Yoruba genre of Nollywood.
Prince Jide Kosoko is a veteran Nollywood pillar whose career spans over five decades across stage, television, and film and is now 72 years old. His daughters, Sola, Bidemi, and Temi Kosoko, are keeping the name in the dynamic industry. Sola Kosoko-Abina and Bidemi Kosoko are both theatre arts graduates who have successfully transitioned into powerhouse actresses, directors, and producers in their own right.
Afro-Juju music singer, Sir Shina Peters, and veteran screen goddess Clarion Chukwura have also contributed to establishing legacy status in the entertainment industry, with their son, Clarence Peters, a reputable music video director who impacts the music industry via his production house, Capital Dreams Pictures.
Also, the Ray Eyiwunmi family, Art Alade, and IK Dairo, who have also left their footprints on planet Earth, have their sons, Muka. Ray, Lasun Ray, Murphy Ray, presently in the movie industry, and Darey, Paul Play Dairo, respectively, are carrying on their father’s legacy in the music industry.
